content.title: About
content.content: Snack mix, plain (Chex Mix) is a dry snack blend made of corn, rice and wheat cereal squares, lightly salted and seasoned with a mild spice mix. It has a crunchy texture and a subtle salty flavor, ideal for on‑the‑go snacking or office breaks.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chex Mix was originally created in the 1950s by General Mills to use up leftover Chex cereal pieces.
The blend often contains a small amount of vegetable oil to help the seasoning adhere to the cereal squares.
It is a popular party snack, often served at movie nights and alongside beer.
The classic recipe uses three types of cereal: rice, corn and wheat Chex.
Many flavor variations exist, but the plain version remains the most neutral.

items.title: Low in added sugar
items.content: The plain Chex Mix contains virtually no added sugar, making it a better choice for those monitoring sugar intake.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: The cereals provide slowly digestible carbohydrates that supply steady energy.

items.title: Contains some fiber
items.content: Rice and wheat squares contribute a modest amount of dietary fiber, supporting digestion.

items.title: B‑vitamin content
items.content: Enriched cereals are a source of B1, B2 and niacin, which help convert food into energy.

items.title: Mineral presence
items.content: Small amounts of iron, magnesium and phosphorus are present in the mix.

items.title: High sodium
items.content: Snack mix is often salted, which can be problematic for people with hypertension or kidney issues.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: The recipe may contain gluten (wheat squares) and soy‑based seasonings; watch for allergies.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Even without sugar, the product is calorie‑dense due to carbs and added oils.

items.title: Vegetable oil content
items.content: Some versions use partially hydrogenated oils that can contain trans fats.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy straight from the bag, toss into salads, use as a crunchy topping for soups, or pair with cheese and dips. For extra crunch, lightly toast in the oven.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place in an airtight container. For longer shelf life, keep refrigerated to prevent oil oxidation.
